newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends sharply higher on export demand.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends sharply higher on export demand.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures ended sharply higher Thursday in response to a jump in demand for wheat, CBOT traders said.
"There's growing world demand for wheat, that is why we're higher," said one CBOT trader.
Wheat markets were filled with talk that Egypt would tender for 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat for February/March shipment, traders said.
However, most exporters said the the Egyptian business would most likely go to Australia or Argentina because of more favorable prices.
In other export business, Sri Lanka tendered for 100,000 hard and soft red wheat for January/February delivery and some exporters believe that half the tender could be supplied by U.S. wheat.
In late trading, Cargill Investor Services bought 400,000 bushels of March, traders said, which helped boost wheat futures near the close, traders said.
CBOT wheat futures closed up two to eight cents per bushel, with March up eight at $3.89-1/4 a bushel and May up 7-1/2 cents at $3.68-1/2.
On the day, Paine Webber sold four million bushels March, Merrill Lynch bought one million March and O'Connor Grain sold 500,000 March in late trade.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, above the 6,128 traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
In options trading, Paine Webber bought 200 March $4.00 calls and sold 200 March $3.50 puts, pit sources said.
